title: XGRIDS ch14/ch18 provisional camera directions (Lab 13S manual visual extrinsics hypothesis test)
recording: Basel House, 2026-07-15-101012-003.xbin (LixelKity K1, software V3.1.1_20250826); extraction run interval-10s

coordinate_convention.world_frame: LAS frame of the scan (Z up, metres). The viewer subtracts the dataset offset (coordinateCenter) for display only; no rotation between LAS and dataset coordinates.

scanner_body_frame.pose_source: poses.csv columns t, x, y, z, qx, qy, qz, qw (scalar last), linearly/SLERP-interpolated to each image timestamp by extract_frames.py
scanner_body_frame.pose_meaning: q rotates body-frame vectors into the LAS frame: v_las = R(q) * v_body; p_las = R(q) * p_body + t
scanner_body_frame.evidence: +X is the walking direction (78% of moving samples within 60 degrees of it); +Z is up (mean 0.98 along world up)

axes.x: optical axis (camera forward, out of the lens)

provisional_camera_frame.note: Same X-forward/Y-left/Z-up convention as the body frame. NOT the OpenCV camera frame (x right, y down, z forward).

to_opencv.description: v_cam = M * v_opencv, i.e. x_cv (right) = -y_cam, y_cv (down) = -z_cam, z_cv (forward) = x_cam

offset_angles.yaw: about body Z; positive = turn RIGHT (clockwise seen from above); -90 = left, +90 = right
offset_angles.pitch: about the yawed Y axis; positive = tilt UP
offset_angles.roll: about the camera's optical axis; positive = CLOCKWISE seen from behind the camera (image up turns toward the right)
offset_angles.rotation_order: intrinsic yaw, then pitch, then roll (Z, Y', X'')
offset_angles.matrix: R_offset = Rz(-yaw) * Ry(-pitch) * Rx(roll), using standard right-handed elementary rotations
offset_angles.three_js: new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(roll, -pitch, -yaw, 'ZYX')) with angles in radians
offset_angles.meaning: R_offset maps provisional-camera-frame vectors into the scanner body frame: v_body = R_offset * v_cam. Its first column is the camera's forward direction in the body frame.
offset_angles.full_chain: v_las = R(q_scanner) * R_offset * v_cam; camera centre = scanner position (lever arm assumed zero)

ch14.uncertainty: about ±10° in yaw and pitch (10° search grid), roll ±10°

ch18.uncertainty: yaw +90 to +105 nearly equally good; pitch ±10°, roll ±10°

best_provisional_offsets.channel_identity: unconfirmed; ch14 looking left is consistent with project.json 'left_main' (index 0), ch18 with 'right_main' (index 2)

test_method.manual: Direction helpers in /camera-calibration compared with the centre of each fisheye image (cross-hair).

numerical.description: Coloured Basel 5M LiDAR rendered through an assumed fisheye at each candidate offset and compared with the real image (grey-level normalised cross-correlation inside the image circle).
numerical.assumed_fisheye_model: equidistant r = f * theta; u = cx + r * (-y_cam / s), v = cy + r * (-z_cam / s), s = sqrt(y_cam^2 + z_cam^2)

equivalent_at_4000x3000.note: assumptions for the test only, not measured intrinsics

numerical.search: yaw every 10° over 360°, pitch -50..+50° every 10°, roll 0; refinement yaw ±10°, pitch ±10°, roll -30..+30° (10° steps) on 5 events
numerical.selection: per event and channel the score is standardised (z-score over the grid); one offset per channel is chosen by the mean z over all events

observations.per_event_note: Single-event peaks are weak in open courtyard views (sky and similar façades on all sides); about 9 of 14 events per channel peak within ±20° of the global offsets. Indoor events are the most distinctive.
qualitative: The operator appears at the left edge of ch14 and the right edge of ch18: for left/right-looking cameras both edges point backward, where the person carrying the scanner is.
1335: ch18 faces the wall with the red-trimmed doorway (renders at +90..+120°); ch14 looks out over the garden (-60..-90°).
2497: ch14 has the veranda on its left and the garden on its right (-90..-120°); ch18 the mirror image (+90..+120°).
4718: ch14 faces the near wall with a louvred window; ch18 looks out over a railing.
observations.conclusion: One fixed offset pair (ch14 left, ch18 right, both level, roll 0) is directionally consistent across the test set. Directions only, to about ±10°.

caveats: Lens model and focal length assumed; image centre approximate.
No lever arm and no camera/pose time offset modelled.
10° search grid (5° in the refinement); 160x120 comparison images.
One recording; other recordings or firmware not checked.
User notes and presets made in the browser are not included; use 'Export notes + presets (JSON)' in /camera-calibration.
